=== sheet 'Sources and notes'
A2='Source: Iwahashi, Masaru 1981, Kinsei Nippon Bukka-shi no Kenkyu, Tokyo Ohara Shinseisha'
A3='(A Study of the History of Price in Early Modern Japan)'
A4='From Appendix Table 1 (pp. 460-465)'
A5='1 Koku = 180.391 liters (Conversion from Russ Rowlett, U. of N.C. at Chapel Hill) '
A9='Osamu Saito (30 July 2008) helpfully clarified the place names and the price-data types for the Iwahashi study:'
A11="1. Osaka: prices at Osaka's Dojima market, of rice produced in Higo, Kyushu."
A12='2. Omi: prices in the town of Otsu, Omi province.'
A13='3. Banshu: rural prices from local sources in southern parts of Banshu province.'
A14="4. Fukuchiyama: prices from Fukuchiyama han documents. This han's castle town is Fukuchiyama."
A15="5. Hiroshima: prices from a Hiroshima merchant's account books. Hiroshima is the castle town of Hiroshima han."
A16="6. Bocho: prices from Choshu han's documents (Choshu han possessed not only Choshu,"
B17='but also an adjacent province; put together, the two provinces were called'
B18='Bocho). The castle town used to be Hagi but in 1865 moved to Yamaguchi.'
A19="7. Saga: prices from Saga han's documents (Saga han's territory covered part of Hizen province, Kyushu). Saga is also its castle town."
A20="8. Kumamoto: prices from Kumamoto han's documents (Kumamoto han's covered Higo province, Kyushu)."
B21='Kumamoto is also the name of its castle town.'
A22='9. Edo: prices in Edo (present-day Tokyo) and environs.'
A23='10. Osaka: As a rice price series, it is the same as entry 1 above. Osaka prices, which were in silver currency, are'
B24='converted into gold ryo with gold-silver ratios at the Osaka market (see Iwahashi 1981, p.277). By dividing series 1'
B25='by series 10, therefore, one should be able to obtain an exchange rate series between the silver-using'
B26='western half and the gold-using eastern half of the country.'
A27="11. Nagoya: prices from Nagoya han's documents (Nagoya han's territory was in Owari province). "
B28='Nagoya is also the name of its castle town.'
A29='12. Shinshu: prices from Ina, an area in southern Shinshu (Shinshu is the name of an inland province).'
A30='13. Aizu: prices in Aizu han, located in the North-east (Tohoku). Wakamatsu (also Aizu-Wakamatsu) is the name of its castle town.'
A31='14. Dewa: prices from Shonai han, which occupied an area in western Dewa (Dewa is the name of a large province '
B32="in the North-east). This han's castle town is called Tsuruoka. "
A34='The nature of price data: Most of the Iwahashi series are not market prices in our usual sense. While series 1 (and 10), '
B35='2 and 3 are undoubtedly derived from market data, others are likely-if not always-to have reflected prices set'
B36='by han government authorities, which were used to convert their rice and cash entries as well as payments. '
B37='Iwahashi (1981) suggests that if averaged out for a reasonably long period, those government-set prices were '
B38='not very different from market price levels, but it is very likely that year-to-year fluctuations were dampened down.'
